input.rationale: With the remaining allocation I am tightening two records rather than opening new work. First, the VerifyLeader question still carries an active disposition although its gap was answered and its current interpretation asserts a scoped defect claim over two executions plus the pre-window controls and their receipt; marking it explained records the boundary honestly, because what remains open is only the isolated near_node_self_voter field of the extended-window harness, which the discriminating experiments refuted as a systematic lag and which cannot change the result (quorumSize and verifyLeader read the leader's own configuration). Second, the extended-window fact rested on a single execution while the repeat receipt f8a32ad3a4de41538ef20a142ae947bc reproduces the same sequence; supplementing its executions with the repeat receipt makes the durable fact rest on two independent executions without changing its statement or conditions.

limitations: The confirmed sequence was observed in two executions of the fixed extended-window experiment and three attempts per receipt in each of two pre-window receipts, all in one process with in-memory transports; the partition is imposed by removing transport routes rather than by a real network failure.
The 20s leader lease is a legal configuration chosen to make the window observable; the claim is about the mechanism and the bound, not the value.

The isolated near_node_self_voter field in the setup events of the extended-window harness (the demoted node's own view still showing the old suffrage) was refuted as a systematic lag by the discriminating experiment and cannot change the result, since the quorum arithmetic and the vote registration both read the leader's own configuration; the field itself remains unexplained and is documented rather than claimed.

knowledge.statement: With voters {L, far1, far2} and non-voter C, per-node timing (L: HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; far1, far2: 3s; C: 6s) and the partition {L, C} | {far1, far2}: L answers VerifyLeader with nil at 0ms after the partition, and answers nil again at 5509ms when one of the far nodes is already Leader, while that node commits a write at index 5 that L's FSM lacks (L still Leader, applied index 3). With the same per-node timing but C still a voter (four voters, quorum 3) no competitor can appear and the same call returns "leadership lost while committing log" at 20003ms, when L's lease expires.
knowledge.conditions: Real 4-node in-memory cluster, only L bootstrapped; near node demoted voter->non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API; transport routes between {L, C} and {far1, far2} removed in both directions; CommitTimeout 200ms; leader lease 20s.

investigations.question: When a leader keeps only a non-voter reachable, does VerifyLeader (the client-visible 'still leader' confirmation) return success even though no quorum of voters replied?
investigations.hypothesis: verifyLeader seeds votes=1 (self) and quorumSize=voters/2+1, then registers the verifyFuture on every followerReplication object, including the ones created for non-voters. A non-voter's successful AppendEntries response reaches notifyAll(true) and increments votes without any suffrage check, so with voters {L,B,D} and non-voter C, L can reach votes==quorumSize==2 with only C's acknowledgement.
investigations.discriminator: Hold topology, partition and timing fixed in a real 4-node in-memory cluster and change exactly one property at a time: (a) demote the node kept with the leader from voter to non-voter through DemoteVoter, (b) keep it a voter, (c) keep it a non-voter but cut the leader from everyone. The prediction is success in (a) and non-success in (b) and (c); the same outcome in (b) or (c) would refute the suffrage-attribution explanation.

gaps.question: Does the false confirmation extend past the leader's own lease window, i.e. does VerifyLeader report success while a different node already holds leadership and has committed a write that the partitioned leader's FSM lacks? The window is bounded because ValidateConfig requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout and checkLeaderLease counts only voters, so the partitioned leader steps down within about one lease interval; a successor harness with per-node timing (long leader lease, short follower election timers) is needed to place a voter-majority election inside that window.

investigations.question: After a committed voter-to-non-voter transition, can a peer's own configuration view keep reporting the old suffrage for seconds while the other peers already report the change, and if so what makes that peer lag on the configuration entry?
investigations.hypothesis: A configuration entry updates a peer's latest configuration only when it is newly appended (appendEntries processes configuration entries of newEntries) or installed through a snapshot; a peer that has not appended the entry keeps reporting its previous configuration. If the leader's replication to one peer stalls - for example a stalled append pipeline that never re-enters RPC mode - that peer would keep the old view while the others commit and apply the change.
investigations.discriminator: Sample every node's own configuration view and LastIndex continuously (for example every 20ms) across the DemoteVoter call and for at least ten seconds afterwards, in the per-node timing used by the extended-window scenario, and repeat the run several times. A peer whose view stays old while its LastIndex also stops advancing would show a replication stall; a peer whose LastIndex has already passed the configuration index while its view stays old would instead point at the configuration-entry processing path; view and index converging within milliseconds in every run would leave the earlier single observation as an unexplained artefact.
counterevidence: Every applicable observation in 0adb78b8f8da429f865c2abb097b4ff8 answers this question negatively for the tested construction: all twelve node observations converged in 0-20ms, and no node had a stale view after its own LastIndex reached the configuration index (indices 4-7, 12-15, 20-23).
The earlier receipt 24679b2ecdd54556adf91882ce0f8b0c carries the same measurements (indices 1-4) with comparisons that were incomplete only because of my admission declaration.
limitations: The refutation is scoped to a healthy, fully connected, unloaded in-memory cluster with this per-node timing; neither contending client traffic nor a deliberately stalled append pipeline was exercised, and the entry-delivery path (appendEntries deciding on newEntries, snapshot install) was traced by reading rather than perturbed.

The sighting that opened the question - near_node_self_voter true after a three second settle loop in receipt 2444815cf0d84e06917efa1091d12257 index 0 - was not reproduced, and its cause is still unidentified; the differences I could name (waiting for followers before the transition, and the per-node timing) were both exercised natively without reproducing it.

investigations.question: When LeadershipTransferToServer names a server that holds no vote, what does the caller observe, what happens to the existing leadership, and does the requested destination ever take leadership?
investigations.hypothesis: initiateLeadershipTransfer does not inspect the target's suffrage, so a non-voter target is contacted with TimeoutNow; timeoutNow makes it a candidate with the leadership-transfer flag and no pre-vote, so it campaigns in the next term. Every voter that receives that RequestVote adopts the higher term and steps down before the suffrage check rejects the vote, so the current leader loses leadership although the target can never win; the transfer future then reports success through the leftLeaderLoop branch, which responds nil without checking whether the requested destination became leader.
investigations.discriminator: Compare the identical call aimed at a non-voter and at a voter in the same 4-node cluster: if the leader merely loses leadership while the requested destination never leads, the suffrage-blind transfer path is established; if the non-voter target leads, or if leadership is unaffected, the explanation is refuted. The control must show that the same call with a voter target results in that target leading.
limitations: One treatment execution and one control, in-memory transports in one process, uniform timings; how long a leaderless interval could last in a cluster with slower timings or fewer reachable voters is not bounded by this receipt.

The caller's observation is the future's error value only; the harness does not distinguish a handover from a fresh election through any other client-visible signal, and it does not read the transfer branch's internal path, so the success is attributed to the lost-leadership branch from the timing pattern (leader already Follower, destination still Candidate) rather than from inside that branch.
The destination is a node demoted through DemoteVoter; AddNonvoter and the deprecated Staging suffrage reach the same Suffrage != Voter path but were not exercised.

knowledge.statement: In a 4-node cluster whose configuration is voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter, LeadershipTransferToServer aimed at the non-voter returns success (nil) within about a millisecond while the sitting leader is already Follower and the named destination is only Candidate; the destination never leads during the following eight seconds and the cluster is observed without a leader at some 20ms sample before a different node wins the fresh election. result.summary: Final record-tightening update, validated and submitted. Two changes: the VerifyLeader question is marked explained now that its gap is answered and its interpretation asserts the scoped claim over two executions of the fixed extended-window experiment plus the pre-window controls, with the residual boundary stated (the isolated near_node_self_voter field of that harness was refuted as a systematic lag by the discriminating experiment and cannot change the result, since the quorum arithmetic and vote registration both read the leader's own configuration); and the extended-window durable fact is supplemented with the repeat receipt f8a32ad3a4de41538ef20a142ae947bc so it rests on two independent executions of the same indices, with its statement, conditions and sources unchanged. The run's three lines are now complete and coherent: VerifyLeader can be confirmed by a non-voter's acknowledgement and stays wrong for the whole configured lease even after another node leads and commits writes the old leader never received (asserted); the suspected demotion view lag was refuted across seven sampled runs and its question closed; and LeadershipTransferToServer aimed at a non-voter reports success indistinguishable from a real handover while the sitting leadership is interrupted and a fresh election decides the outcome, bounded by the observed recovery (asserted). No further experiment was submitted, since the remaining allocation would not cover executing and interpreting another receipt.
